jobs.description:
A Snapshot of Your Day 

As Program Lead Finance (f/m/d), you lead the Finance transformation for Large Steam & Syncons (LSS) while serving as co-lead of the overall LSS rollout within Siemens Energy's global S4Energy program.
In this project-driven Engineer-to-Order (ETO) business, you act as the key Finance & Controlling representative, ensuring that business requirements are translated into scalable SAP S/4HANA solutions. Working closely with Finance, Controlling, Manufacturing, and global program teams, you steer critical decisions across project controlling, product costing, manufacturing controlling, and financial closing.
From shaping target processes and driving testing activities to coordinating cutover, go-live, and change management, you combine strategic leadership with hands-on execution to deliver a successful and sustainable business transformation.

How You’ll Make an Impact 

* Lead the Finance transformation and co-lead the S4Energy rollout for Large Steam & Syncons, ensuring alignment across stakeholders and program objectives
* Drive end-to-end Finance implementation activities, including requirements management, process design, Fit-Gap workshops, testing, data migration, cutover, go-live, and hypercare
* Harmonize Finance & Controlling processes by balancing business requirements with SAP S/4HANA standards and scalable best practices
* Coordinate cross-functional rollout activities and manage dependencies across Finance, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, and IT
* Build and leverage a global Siemens Energy transformation network to share best practices and accelerate implementation success
* Lead stakeholder engagement and change management initiatives to ensure organizational readiness and sustainable adoption

What You Bring

* Bachelor's or Master's degree in Business Administration, Finance, Accounting, Information Systems, or a related field
* Extensive experience in SAP S/4HANA Finance & Controlling, including leading complex implementation and business transformation programs
* Strong expertise in Record-to-Report, Project Controlling, Product Costing, Manufacturing Controlling, and Financial Closing
* Solid understanding of Engineer-to-Order (ETO) business processes and end-to-end value flows across project execution and manufacturing
* Excellent stakeholder management, analytical thinking, and leadership skills with experience aligning global cross-functional teams
* Fluency in German and English, enabling effective collaboration in an international environment

About the Team

Our Gas Services division offers Low-emission power generation through service and 
decarbonization. Zero or low emission power generation and all gas turbines under one roof, 
steam turbines and generators. Decarbonization opportunities through service offerings, 
modernization, and digitalization of the fleet. 

Who is Siemens Energy? 

At Siemens Energy, we are more than just an energy technology company. With ~100.000 dedicated employees in more than 90 countries, we develop the energy systems of the future, ensuring that the growing energy demand of the global community is met reliably and sustainably. The technologies created in our research departments and factories drive the energy transition and provide the base for one sixth of the world's electricity generation.

Our global team is committed to making sustainable, reliable, and affordable energy a reality by pushing the boundaries of what is possible. We uphold a 150-year legacy of innovation that encourages our search for people who will support our focus on decarbonization, new technologies, and energy transformation.      

Find out how you can make a difference at Siemens Energy: https://www.siemens-energy.com/employeevideo

Our Commitment to Diversity 

Lucky for us, we are not all the same. Through diversity we generate power. We run on inclusion and our combined creative energy is fueled by over 130 nationalities. Siemens Energy celebrates character – no matter what ethnic background, gender, age, religion, identity, or disability. We energize society, all of society, and we do not discriminate based on our differences. 

Rewards/Benefits 

* In addition to an attractive remuneration package in line with the market, you can expect an attractive employer-financed company pension scheme
* We also offer the opportunity to become a Siemens Energy shareholder
* We offer our employees the opportunity to work flexibly and remotely, and our inspiring offices provide space for collaboration and creativity
* The professional and personal development of our employees is very important to us. We provide them with the opportunities to learn and develop in a self-determined way, various attractive programmes and learning materials are available for this purpose
* In relation to the "compatibility of family and work", we have a wide range of offers, e.g. flexible working time models, childcare places at many locations, the possibility of trial part-time work or even a sabbatical

Place of work: Production site, near Chemnitz, Germany
Start date: ASAP

About us

We’re on a mission to revolutionize how the world produces protein and we’re just getting started.

Pacifico is a Leipzig-based biotech company producing the world’s most cost-competitive texturized protein through fermentation. Our technology makes sustainable, high-quality protein cheaper than conventional meat production – not just better for the planet, but better for you.

Our production site near Chemnitz is where science meets scale: industrial fermentation systems, food-grade processing lines, and a team that moves fast. We’re now looking for a Process Operator (f/m/d) to support the day-to-day facility operations at our production site.

The role

In this role, you will support the operations of our fermentation facility and all related processing steps. You will work closely with a Senior Process Lead and will be trained on our equipment, processes, and quality standards.

The role is strongly hands-on and operational, with a focus on running equipment, preparing materials, and supporting production. Working hours are initially within typical daytime working hours; as production scales, openness to late and occasional weekend shifts is valued.

Your main tasks

- Preparation of fermentation media (weighing, mixing, heating, handling raw materials)
- Operating fermentation tanks and auxiliary equipment
- Supporting downstream processing (emptying tanks, handling and processing biomass)
- Operating our food processing line and its associated equipment
- Monitoring basic process parameters (e.g. temperature, time, filling levels)
- Cleaning and sanitising equipment (CIP systems and manual cleaning)
- Maintaining cleanliness, order, and safety in the facility
- Documenting basic production activities and flagging issues when they arise

Your profile

- Practical experience in food & beverage or similar manufacturing environments
- Comfortable working in a production setting with physical tasks and machinery
- Careful, reliable, and quality-oriented working style
- Interest in food production and fermentation processes
- Ability to work well in a small team and communicate clearly on the shop floor
- Basic working knowledge of English

Nice to have

- Experience in a brewery, dairy or fermentation-based production
- Technical or vocational training in a relevant field
- Familiarity with hygiene standards and food safety practices
- Experience with CIP systems or industrial cleaning routines
- Basic working knowledge of German

What we offer

- A full-time role with clear responsibilities and growth opportunities
- 28 days of paid holiday per year
- Subsidy for the Germany Ticket (“Deutschland-Ticket”)
- Hands-on training and close collaboration with experienced colleagues

How to apply

A short CV/brief overview of your previous work experience is sufficient.

A focus of our research are Engineered Living Materials (ELMs), an emergent class of materials at the interface between materials science and synthetic biology, with huge potential for sustainable innovation in different technological fields. The multidisciplinary component of our research requires intensive information and data exchange between multiple disciplines. We work on semantically structured data and interfaces, AI-driven workflows, and contribute to engaging the growing ELM community in digitalized research.

To support the digitalization of SynBio work within the context of ELM development, we are seeking a

Postdoctoral Researcher with expertise in Synthetic Biology (f/m/d)

and interest in data-driven research. The position is integrated in the collaborative network MaterialVital Hub, recently funded by the Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space (BMFTR) in collaboration with the Galaxy Community Hub. The candidate will be part of a team of experimental scientists and research data management experts at INM-Leibniz Institute for New Materials and Bioinformaticians at the University of Freiburg.

Your roles:

- Contribute to the digitalization of synthetic biology workflows for ELM development in collaboration with SynBio researchers at INM.
- Develop metadata schemas for typical synthetic biology steps and methodologies in ELM research which are transferable to electronic LabBooks and data platforms of relevance for other researchers within the MaterialVital Hub.
- Contribute to the development of an ELM-dedicated ontology for interoperability within the MaterialVital Hub in cooperation with MaterialDigital Platform partners and the Galaxy Community Hub.
- Support and promote digitalization of the ELM community within the MaterialVital Hub in close interaction with Galaxi Community Hub and MaterialDigital Platform and NFDI.
- Attend workshops and disseminate your work within the ELM community by presenting at conferences and scientific events.
- Document your work and report to project coordinators and stakeholders.

Your profile:

- PhD degree in synthetic biology, biotechnology or related disciplines.

We are looking to support our rapidly growing team as soon as possible: Postdoctoral Researcher (f/m/x) Biology (Life Sciences) for Preclinical Imaging

Radiochemie TV-L: 38,5 h/week (100%) 1-year fixed-term contract under the WissZeitVG; plus a 1-year extension for a third-party funded project
Your salary will be based on TV-L

Your tasks
• Planning, conducting and analyzing the biological evaluation of newly developed PET and SPECT radiotracers
• Contributing to the establishment, optimization and
documentation of biological test systems and preclinical evaluation protocols
• Performing in vitro studies, including stability, binding and cellular uptake assays as well as studies using models of the blood-brain-barrier
• Preclinical evaluation of tracer candidates in suitable in vivo models, including support of small-animal imaging studies
• Performing and analyzing ex vivo studies, e.g., autoradiography, biodistribution studies and complementary tissue analyses
• Quantitative analysis of biological and imaging data and
interpretation of results in close interaction with the other project partners
• Evaluation, documentation, and scientific presentation of experimental results in project reports, publications, and presentations

Your profile
• Completed university degree and Ph.D. in biology, life sciences, neuroscience, biochemistry, pharmacy or a related field
• Experience in preclinical imaging (e.g. small animal PET, SPECT, MRI, CT)
• Experience with animal models and experimental animal work is advantageous (FELASA-B or EU functions A, C, D)
• Experience with cell culture, in vitro assays, autoradiography, ex vivo analyses and BBB models is desirable
• Interest in radiopharmaceutical tracer development, molecular imaging and translational research
• Willingness to work with unsealed radioactive substances and to become familiar with radiation protection-related workflows
• Willingness to conduct biological and preclinical experiments within an interdisciplinary team
• Good written and spoken English skills
• Structured, independent and conscientious working style
• Ability to work in a team, strong communication skills and interest in interdisciplinary collaboration between chemistry, radiochemistry, biology, medicine and imaging

Our offer
• Everything but ordinary: You can expect a secure job in a challenging, innovative environment – including company pension schemes and regular working hours without business trips.
• Work-life balance: Whether full-time or part-time, with or without children – with numerous support options, we will find the right path together.
• Team spirit in R(h)ine culture: You will be warmly welcomed by an interdisciplinary team that values mutual respect and helpfulness.
• Strong perspectives: We offer extensive training opportunities – so you can continuously grow and set new goals.

Your future with us
We are one of the leading university hospitals in Germany and network research, teaching and health care at the highest level. That's why many things are a lot bigger for us: the spectrum of exciting development opportunities. The limitless openness with which specialists from all over the world work together here. Or our commitment as an employer to support all employees as best we can in reconciling their job with their goals and life situations.
This is the University Hospital of Cologne: Everything but ordinary.

Your future in detail
The Institute of Radiochemistry and Experimental Molecular Imaging (IREMB) is seeking a postdoctoral researcher for a translational research project in the field of radiopharmaceutical tracer development and molecular imaging. The postdoc position will initially be embedded for one year in the internationally funded IMAGESTRO project. There is an option of extension for another year. The focus of the work will be on the biological validation of newly developed PET or SPECT radiotracers.
The IMAGESTRO project aims to develop novel 18F-labeled PET tracers for the non-invasive imaging of estrogen receptors in the brain, to characterize them preclinically, and to translate them into human applications. The project focuses on the organic synthesis of suitable precursor and reference compounds, the development and optimization
of radiofluorination strategies, and the comprehensive analytical and preclinical characterization of the resulting radiotracers. The work will be carried out in close cooperation between the University Hospital Cologne and Forschungszentrum Jülich and offers an interdisciplinary research environment at the interface of organic chemistry, radiochemistry, radiopharmacy, molecular imaging, biology and neuroscience.

• Build and refine a simulation framework for synthetic patient trajectories
• Design and analyse virtual perturbation scenarios to investigate resilience and transition dynamics

• Contribute to the implementation of a research prototype and reusable open resources

• Strong interest in mental health research and interdisciplinary collaboration with clinical partners
• A structured, independent, and reliable way of working combined with strong team skills

• A solid publication record appropriate to career stage is desirable

Your future in detail

We are looking to support a newly established research group as soon as possible.
The position is embedded in the third-party funded research project SiReD-MH (Tipping Minds: Simulation of Resilience Dynamics in Mental Health). The project develops a hybrid in-silico framework to model resilience dynamics and transitions into mental illness in young people at risk. Using longitudinal digital phenotyping data, including ecological momentary assessment, actigraphy, and GPS-derived mobility measures, the project combines generative machine learning and simulation to build synthetic patient trajectories and test resilience under virtual perturbation scenarios.

TheInstitute of Transfusion Medicine and Cellular Therapeutics (https://www.ukaachen.de/kliniken-institute/transfusionsmedizin-blutspendedienst/transfusionsmedizin/) is seeking

- 
Generation and expansion of hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) &

- 
Translation control in the hematopoietic system

Operational area: Institute of Transfusion Medicine and Cellular Therapeutics

Working hours: 65% of the collectively agreed full-time working hours (currently 38.5 hours per week)

Duration/Term of employment: Initially limited to 3 years. The position offers the opportunity to pursue a doctoral degree

Start date: As soon as possible

Remuneration/Rates: EG 13 (TV-L)

Why you should choose us?

We offer…

- 30 days of vacation per year for full-time employment
- A bonus of 3,000 euros for employees who help recruit employees in different sectors
- An attractive company pension scheme from VBL
- Education opportunities, including updating and upgrading
- Access to public transport
- In-house kindergarten (places subject to availability)
- Staff residences (places subject to availability and by arrangement)
- An onboarding app for new employees
- Extended opening hours in the staff restaurant

Description

At the Institute of Transfusion Medicine and Cellular Therapeutics (Director: Univ.-Prof. Dr. Hannes Klump) we investigate mRNA-based reprogramming hematopoietic cells. Our aims are to generate and expand hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) and to produce novel cellular therapeutics for patient care. We further investigate the regulation of translation in resting HSCs and during their differentiation into the hematopoietic lineages, as well as stimulation-induced changes to translation in mature hematopoietic cells. Our aim is to gain unprecedented and molecular insight into the underlying genetic programs and mechanisms and to leverage this understanding for the generation of novel therapeutic approaches.

In close collaboration with our research partners, we employ multidisciplinary approaches combining chemical synthesis, cell biology, molecular genetics, and biochemistry. We further offer an outstanding, international research environment with state-of-the-art facilities located in a newly constructed building that houses spacious clean rooms.

Your profile

- We are seeking strong candidates with a master’s degree in biology, biotechnology, biochemistry, or a related field with excellent academic records. Applicants should bring experience in molecular biology and the culture of human cells; experience in flow cytometry is a plus. Excellent communication skills and proficiency in the English language (Level C1), both written and spoken, are required.
- We offer close mentorship by experienced researchers and a vibrant working environment that fosters innovation and interdisciplinary collaboration for academic and professional growth
